items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Some jazz fans got the news that some American Negro jazz musicians were in town so they came to see us

ctx.x: Everything went fine and the 25th of February we left Alexandria on a small Italian ship called Egeo. We stopped at the Island of Rhodes which we had time to visit. The next stop, [was] Oireens, Greece and we visited Athens. It was a three-day trip from Alexandria to Naples and we were obliged to stay in Naples

five days before we had a ship to New York. We met an Italian sailor and a civilian who became friendly with us and showed us around the city, took us to some restaurants where we could eat good and not pay too much. The sailor went AWOL and spent every day with us. We had to report to the American Embassy where our passports were cancelled for any further trips to Europe. Some jazz fans got the news that some American Negro jazz musicians were in town so they came to see us and one of them invited us to his home…

We left Naples the 5th of March 1940 on the Italian liner Saturna and the trip was eleven days. We jammed most every night with the musicians that played in first class and they were really happy because it gave them a chance to get some ideas about jazz, which they liked but seldom had a chance to play or listen to, except on receords and in some clubs in New York where the ship would stay for three days, to take on supplies for the return crossing back to Naples.
